place_name: Cascade Canyon, Grand Teton National Park, WY
approach_stated: Boat across Jenny Lake then horse trail; Baxter's Pinnacle 'about a 1/2 hr approach if you take the boat'; without boat 2.6 mi around lake (or 1.7 mi from String Lake) before the canyon trail; Guide's Wall further up canyon (time not stated)
summit_or_glacier: Baxter's Pinnacle routes finish on the pinnacle summit; Guide's Wall is a 'non-summit' Grade II 6-pitch route

evidence.fact: Approach options: boat across Jenny Lake, hike 2.6 miles around the lake, or 1.7 miles from String Lake lot.
About a 1/2 hr approach if you take the boat; double cracks lead to the summit. Type Trad, Alpine, 5 pitches.
Guide's Wall is a classic Teton non-summit rock climb, Trad, Alpine, 6 pitches, Grade II.

note: Mixed area in a national-park backcountry canyon reached by boat or 1.7-2.6 mi of lakeshore trail; Baxter's routes summit a pinnacle. Guide's Wall/Attritus/Bat Attack/Vieux Guide share Guide's Wall approach deeper in canyon, time not stated - kept alpine; per-route split possible.

place_name: Main Wall, The Halidome, Empire, CO
approach_stated: Allow 20-25 minutes for the approach (to The Catwalk); road-side parking 3.2 mi north of Empire
summit_or_glacier: No summit; routes climb a 500+ ft roadside crag (top over 10,000 ft) to the Catwalk ledge/top of crag; no snow/glacier

evidence.fact: Allow 20-25 minutes for the approach; the crag sits several hundred feet above the road, 3.2 miles west of Empire.
From Empire proceed north 3.2 miles; parking on both sides of the road for the next 0.5 miles.

note: Multi-pitch (to 6 pitches, Grade III) crag with a short walk; MP tags Alpine for the 10,000 ft setting only.

place_name: The Main Wall, Bear Creek Wall, Lost River Range, ID
approach_stated: The walk is about 40 minutes (from wherever the road is legally drivable)
summit_or_glacier: No summit or glacier; 2-3 pitch crag routes

evidence.fact: The crag is plainly obvious and the walk is about 40 minutes; four sections incl. Lower Tier and The Main Wall.
Chert Albert: Trad, 250 ft, 3 pitches.

note: Road end condition uncertain (author has not driven it in two decades). MP does not tag these routes Alpine.

place_name: Myrtle 2 aka "Turtle Arches", Boundary County, North Idaho
approach_stated: Hike/bike the old road/trail about an hour (2.3 mi) from Two Mouth Lakes TH (#268), then about 10-15 min (1/3 mi) on game trail to the dome
summit_or_glacier: No summit/glacier; up to 4-pitch (500 ft) dome routes, walk/scramble off or rappel

evidence.fact: Hike/bike up the old road/trail for about an hour (2.3 miles); then about 10-15 minutes (1/3 mile) from trail #268.
FJL: Trad, Alpine, 500 ft, 4 pitches; walk/scramble off left or rappel with 2 ropes.

note: Stated approach ~70-75 min (exceeds 60) after 12 mi of gravel FS road; borderline, kept alpine on the stated time.

place_name: The Bud Wall, Wolverine Bowl, Bridger Range, MT
approach_stated: 1 hour hike from the Bracket Creek lot to the Wolverine meadow (45 min if hiking quickly), then climbers trail past Lower and Upper Replica to the wall (time not stated)
summit_or_glacier: No summit/glacier; single-pitch sport routes 55-115 ft

evidence.fact: From the parking lot it is a 1 hour hike to Wolverine (45min if hiking quickly).
From the meadow follow the climbers trail past Lower and Upper Replica; first route is Boy Scout Hand Grenade.

note: Borderline: ~45-60 min to the meadow plus a short unstated trail; single-pitch sport cliff, so crag. The Beat Connection not listed on MP area page.

place_name: Summer Triangle (aka Upper Replica), Wolverine Bowl, Bridger Range, MT
approach_stated: 1 hour hike to the Wolverine meadow (45 min if hiking quickly), then a short climbers trail past the Lower Replica (time not stated)
summit_or_glacier: No summit/glacier; single-pitch sport routes 85-100 ft

evidence.fact: From the parking lot it is a 1 hour hike to Wolverine (45min if hiking quickly).
From the meadow follow the climbers trail along the Lower Replica, across a small scree field to the Upper Replica.

note: Borderline like Bud Wall (slightly closer). The Hanging Garden not listed on MP area page.

place_name: Cirque of the Moon, Wind River Range, WY
approach_stated: About 12 miles in from Dickinson Park; ~15 miles one way from Big Sandy trailhead (most recent parties approach via Cirque of the Towers)
summit_or_glacier: Roadless wilderness cirque; Grade III-V walls up to 13 pitches

evidence.fact: Compact horseshoe of walls about 12 miles in from Dickinson Park; from Big Sandy ~15 miles one way.
Mare Frigoris: Trad, Aid, Alpine, 1300 ft, 13 pitches, Grade V.

note: Correctly alpine: multi-day backcountry approach.

place_name: Bionut Wall, Flowing Park, Grand Mesa, CO
approach_stated: From the reservoir parking take Mesa Top Trail 714 about five minutes to a fire pit, then a faint trail a few paces to the cliff; area described as 'a short approach'
summit_or_glacier: No summit/glacier; ~50 ft single-pitch basalt rim

evidence.fact: Averages around 50 feet tall, gear and bolts, short approach; Mesa Top Trail about five minutes to a fire pit.
This is the main wall first encountered on approach.

note: Clear crag (single pitch 40-50 ft).

place_name: Possibility Slab, Possibility Area, Mt Blue Sky (Mt Evans), CO
approach_stated: Base: 2.75 mi from Echo Lake via Chicago Lakes trail ('a long hike'); alternative 0.75 mi from a Mt Blue Sky Road pullout to a notch, then two 35 m rappels in (time not stated)
summit_or_glacier: No summit; high-alpine slab (Mt Blue Sky), climb-out finish at the rim

evidence.fact: Road approach 0.75 miles with raps; Chicago Creek Trail approach 2.75 miles; drawbacks include a long hike.
From the notch do two 35 meter raps down The Upsides to reach the base.

note: No time stated; kept alpine for the 2.75 mi basin approach / rap-in access above treeline. Could be judged crag if the 0.75 mi rap-in is treated as the approach.

place_name: Cowen Massif (Mt Cowen and the Eenie/Meenie/Minie/Moe towers), Absaroka Range, Paradise Valley, MT
approach_stated: Elbow Lake trail ~8 miles, 4-5 hours usually required; then about an hour from a camp at Elbow Lake into the east fork to the routes
summit_or_glacier: Summit finishes: Go West 'Spectacular summit', Conscious Water 'goes direct to the summit', Centennial Route reaches the true summit; Grade II-IV, 7-12 pitches

evidence.fact: The trail to the lake is ~8 miles. 4-5 hours is usually required; camp at Elbow Lake.
About an hour approach into the east fork of Elbow Creek from a camp at Elbow Lake; spectacular summit.

note: Correctly alpine: overnight backcountry approach and summit finishes.

place_name: Henderson's Buttress, Cannon Cliff, Franconia Notch, NH
approach_stated: Not timed: take the Whitney-Gilman Ridge trail then a faint trail left below the ridge; Cannon described as 'a long talus approach'; Whitney-Gilman approach starts 7-8 min along the paved path then woods and talus
summit_or_glacier: No summit/glacier; routes up to 700 ft / 7 pitches top out on the buttress and walk off to the trail

evidence.fact: Take the Whitney-Gilman Ridge Trail until you can go left below ridge, then a faint trail.
A long talus approach leads to the base; parking on the north end of the cliff off I-93.
Walk the paved path about 7-8 min to a path on the right, then through woods and talus to the ridge base.

note: Roadside (I-93) cliff, no summit, but total approach time never stated on pages read; likely crag-length but not verified.

place_name: Big Wall, Cannon Cliff, Franconia Notch, NH
approach_stated: Not timed: 'Hike the Moby Grape trail and head left'; Cannon has 'a long talus approach'; Moby Grape page gives only return times (descent ~20 min + ~15 min back to the start)
summit_or_glacier: No glacier; long Grade III-V routes to the top of the cliff (Benedictus 'Finale pitch to the summit' of the cliff); 1000 ft wall

evidence.fact: Getting There: Hike the Moby Grape trail and head left.
Walk down the descent trail about 20 minutes; from there about 15 minutes walk back to the start.
A long talus approach leads to the base and can be heinous if wet or snow covered.

note: Roadside big wall with Grade IV-V routes; approach-to-base time not stated. Descent figures suggest under an hour but not stated as approach.

place_name: Melting Mud West, East Hellgate, Little Cottonwood Canyon, UT
approach_stated: Cairned climber's trail from across the Alta Peruvian Lodge, about 5 minutes of steep switchbacking to the Melting Mud Wall
summit_or_glacier: No summit/glacier; single-pitch sport 70-105 ft

evidence.fact: A cairn marked climber's trail takes about 5 minutes of steep switchbacking to reach the Melting Mud Wall.
Getting there: same as all East Hellgate climbs.

note: Clear crag. The Rise of Punk not listed on the MP area page.

place_name: Trail Lake Pinnacle, Far Northern Winds (near Dubois), WY
approach_stated: Not timed: from the road pullout at the head of Trail Lake, 'hike steeply uphill to the west until the pinnacle towers overhead'
summit_or_glacier: The pinnacle has a summit (register, rap anchor) but the sample routes are 30-40 ft crack/sport lines on the lower-left buttress, not summit routes

evidence.fact: From the pullout at the head of Trail Lake, hike steeply uphill to the west until the pinnacle towers overhead.
Clean Cut, 40 ft: on the lower-left buttress split by several large cracks (YTP, Behemoth).

note: Road-accessible and the samples are single-pitch 30-40 ft cragging, so likely crag, but no approach time/distance stated. The Wide One not on MP area page.

place_name: Warbonnet Peak, Cirque of the Towers, Wind River Range, WY
approach_stated: 'An arduous hike in over Jackass Pass from the Big Sandy trailhead' (multi-mile backcountry; time not stated)
summit_or_glacier: Summit finishes ('views of the Cirque from the summit'; 'easier ground to summit'); Grade III-IV, up to 10 pitches

evidence.fact: An arduous hike in over Jackass Pass from the Big Sandy trailhead.
Northeast Face Left: Trad, Alpine, 1100 ft, Grade III; views of the Cirque from the summit are spectacular.

note: Correctly alpine.

place_name: Highlands Wall, Crystal Crag, Lake George, Mammoth Lakes, CA
approach_stated: Crystal Crag approach takes about 45 minutes from the Lake George lot; Highlands Wall is the first cliff reached on that approach
summit_or_glacier: No summit for these routes (a couple of other Crystal Crag routes reach the summit); single-pitch sport 90-100 ft

evidence.fact: Park at Lake George, Crystal Lake Trail; the approach takes about 45 minutes.
Highlands Wall is the first cliff you will see as you approach Crystal Crag; visible from the parking lot.

note: Clear crag: single-pitch sport, <=45 min.

place_name: Right of the Regular Route, The Plug (Lassen Peak), Lassen Volcanic NP, CA
approach_stated: Lassen Peak trail ~1.1 mi then off-trail boulder field (or snow); 'The approach can take anywhere from 60-90 minutes', descent as long
summit_or_glacier: On the flank of Lassen Peak; routes top out on the crag ('up to the summit of the crag') with an ugly talus/scree walk-off; snow possible on approach

evidence.fact: Approach required by the Park Service; the approach can take anywhere from 60-90 minutes; descent can take as long.
P4 chase the crack up to the summit of the crag; walk off is loose talus/scree.

note: Correctly alpine (60-90 min stated). The Great Hot Blast not on MP area page.

place_name: First and Second Terrace, The Plug (Lassen Peak), Lassen Volcanic NP, CA
approach_stated: Same Park-Service-required approach to The Plug: ~1.1 mi on Lassen Peak trail then boulder field; 60-90 minutes
summit_or_glacier: Lassen Peak flank, snow possible on approach; single-pitch 90-160 ft terrace routes

evidence.fact: The approach can take anywhere from 60-90 minutes; long approach and descent make for a full day.
Getting there: see previous area (Belly Button / The Plug).

note: Alpine on stated 60-90 min approach.

place_name: Eagle Lake Buttress, Eagle Creek Canyon, Lake Tahoe West Shore (Desolation Wilderness), CA
approach_stated: The approach takes roughly 1.5 hours and gains roughly 1600 ft over 2 miles from Eagle Falls TH
summit_or_glacier: Summit finishes (Wind Tree 'cracks to the summit', Orange Book onto the summit block; Tom sans Bob on the real summit); low 5th downclimb or rap off

evidence.fact: The approach to Eagle Lake Buttress takes roughly 1.5 hours and gains roughly 1600' over 2 miles.
Wind Tree: Trad, Alpine, 3 pitches; traverse right and head up cracks to the summit.

note: Correctly alpine (90 min + summit).

place_name: Lower Tier, Bear Creek Wall, Lost River Range, ID
approach_stated: The walk to Bear Creek Wall is about 40 minutes; the Lower Tier is the first bit of rock reached, right below the main cliff
summit_or_glacier: No summit/glacier; single-pitch (80 ft) sport and trad

evidence.fact: The crag is plainly obvious and the walk is about 40 minutes.
It's the first bit of rock you get to, right below the main cliff.

note: Clear crag; MP does not tag these Alpine at all.

place_name: Yucca Flower Tower, Echo Canyon, Sandia Mountains, NM
approach_stated: Sandia Crest Spur trail 0.5 mi to the La Luz junction, then 10 minutes (~0.3 mi) on La Luz, short climber trail and rap in; Echo Canyon has 'one of the shortest approaches in the Sandia Mountains'
summit_or_glacier: Routes top out on the small tower's summit just off the La Luz Trail (not a mountain summit); no snow/glacier

evidence.fact: Echo Canyon has one of the shortest approaches in the Sandias; Crest Spur trail to La Luz junction (.5 miles).
From the trail junction, continue 10 minutes or about 0.3 miles on the main trail, then climber trail and rap approach.

note: Top-down crag from Sandia Crest parking; tower summit is a crag top. MP lists no Alpine tag.

place_name: Watchtower, Pinnacle Valley, Sandia Mountains (West Side), NM
approach_stated: Not timed: from the last hairpin below Sandia Crest, 0.2 mi to a trail junction, along North Crest Trail and a boot path down to ~10,173 ft, fixed handline then three 35 m rappels to the base; climb out
summit_or_glacier: No summit/glacier; rappel-in, climb-out formation, routes to 340 ft / 4 pitches

evidence.fact: Rappel in and climb out; trail junction 0.2 miles from parking, boot path down, then three 35 m rappels.
Seventh Sojourn: Trad, 340 ft, 4 pitches, Grade III.

note: Road-accessed top-down crag; no approach time or total distance stated, so unsure. MP lists no Alpine tag. Sword in the Stone not on MP area page.

place_name: Omega Buttress, Death Canyon, Grand Teton National Park, WY
approach_stated: A little over 2 mi on the Death Canyon trail, ~0.5 mi up canyon, talus, 4th-class gully then 10-15 min more; 'Total approach time is about 1 1/2 hour' (Death Canyon generally 60-90 min)
summit_or_glacier: No summit/glacier; Grade II-III 2-5 pitch routes, rappel/gully descent

evidence.fact: Total approach time is about 1 1/2 hour; 4th class terrain in a loose gully to the base.
Relatively short approach (60 to 90 minutes) for most of the routes.
Sherm's Crack, 40 ft, on a small buttress by the approach gully; approx 1hr from Death Canyon TH.

note: Stated 90 min > 60, so alpine by the rule, though MP calls it 'not overly alpine in nature'. Sherm's Crack alone is ~1 hr.

place_name: Ambush Peak, East Fork Valley, Wind River Range, WY
approach_stated: From Big Sandy TH via Dad's, Marm's and Pyramid Lakes and around Midsummer Dome; East Fork Valley 'hike 14 miles'
summit_or_glacier: 1600 ft face 'leading to a summit'; routes finish on the summit ridge; Grade III-IV, 10-16 pitches

evidence.fact: Start at Big Sandy Opening and hike 14 miles.
800 ft slabby apron then 800 ft of steep terrain leading to a summit; walk-off to the south.

note: Correctly alpine.

place_name: The Real Cloud Ripper Tower, Cloud Ripper Towers, Tahquitz 'Others', Idyllwild, CA
approach_stated: Not timed: 'Follow death march as if you are going to Hinterland Buttress' (around Tahquitz via the North Gully area); parent area says 'Mucho hiking'
summit_or_glacier: No glacier; small wedge-shaped towers/mini crags, 70-230 ft Grade II routes, walk off

evidence.fact: Follow death march as if going to Hinterland Buttress; towers are smaller wedge-shaped mini crags to the east.
Getting There: Mucho hiking.

note: Approach described only as a 'death march' behind Tahquitz; likely >60 min but no time or distance stated.

place_name: Castle Grey Skull, Forest Road 2N86, Big Bear Lake, CA
approach_stated: 'Surprisingly fun little crag that has a short 5-10 min approach' from the end of FR 2N86
summit_or_glacier: No summit/glacier; 30-50 ft single pitch

evidence.fact: Surprisingly fun little crag that has a short 5-10 min approach.
From Hwy 18 / Mill Creek Road drive 3.9 miles and turn right onto Forest Road 2N86.

note: Clear crag.

place_name: Karst Crag, Marble Mountain (Marble Mountain Wilderness), Northwest California
approach_stated: Reached on foot from Lover's Camp Trailhead via the PCT, then 0.3 mi along the Marble Gap Trail; total hiking distance/time from the trailhead not stated
summit_or_glacier: No summit/glacier; 65-70 ft single-pitch marble routes in a roadless wilderness; MP calls Marble Mountain 'perhaps the most neglected alpine climbing location in California'

evidence.fact: After turning off the PCT onto the Marble Gap Trail, continue another .3 miles and the wall is on your left.
Perhaps the most neglected alpine climbing location in California; drive to Lover's Camp Trailhead.

note: Alpine on roadless-backcountry grounds (wilderness, reached via PCT); the walk length is not stated on MP, so a second source with the mileage would firm this up.

place_name: Lower East Face, Longs Peak, Rocky Mountain National Park, CO
approach_stated: Longs Peak trailhead to Chasm Lake 4.5 mi, then more to the rock; at least 5 miles
summit_or_glacier: Mill's Glacier snow crossing typical (ice axe useful); routes reach Broadway with option to continue via Kiener's to the Longs summit; Grade II-IV

evidence.fact: Hike to Chasm Lake, 4.5 mi, then more; typically a section of snow (Mill's Glacier), ice axe useful.
Most common approach from the Longs Peak trailhead will be at least 5 miles.

note: Correctly alpine. Diagonal Direct, Overhang Dihedral and Shining Slab are not listed under this MP area (types not read).

place_name: East Gully, North Side, Garden Creek Gap, East Idaho
approach_stated: Roadside: park at pullouts outside the gap, walk west into the gap and take the climber's trail where the first fin touches the road, around the buttress into the first gully (no time stated)
summit_or_glacier: No summit/glacier; 40-100 ft single-pitch sport and trad

evidence.fact: Walk west into the Gap; climber's trail starts just before the first fin touches the road.
The first gully coming into the gap from the East.

note: Roadside crag at the road's edge; approach time not given in minutes but the cliff begins at the road.

place_name: Main Wall, Eagle Cliff (Hounds Hump Ridge), Franconia Notch, NH
approach_stated: About a 40 to 50 minute uphill hike: Greenleaf Trail 30-40 min from the Old Man of the Mountain site, then climber's trail about 10 min
summit_or_glacier: No summit/glacier; single-pitch 75-120 ft routes

evidence.fact: About a 40 to 50 minute uphill hike via the Greenleaf Trail then a climber's trail.
About a 50 minute uphill hike: Greenleaf Trail about 40 minutes, climber's trail about 10 minutes.

note: Crag at <=50 min; two consistent MP statements.
